faq.q: How does the robot plan routes?
alts: how does the robot avoid obstacles
faq.text: The robot plans routes with an A* search on a virtual floor map, using 8-connected cells with no corner cutting, a step limit of 0.18 m, and a cost that keeps it centered in aisles [DOC-APP-NAV]. A cell is walkable only if it is observed floor and has more than 0.20 m of clearance from the distance transform, and the path is then smoothed only inside walkable cells [DOC-APP-NAV]. The route is validated by resampling about every 2.5 cm and checking for collisions and minimum clearance [DOC-APP-NAV].

faq.q: What can I ask the copilot?
alts: how do I use the copilot
faq.text: You can ask about the plant in a few ways: locate objects in the scan, find an asset with an abnormal signal, find the faulty or highest-priority asset, open a diagnosis, send the robot, open the X-Ray view, or use Learn, Practice, or the library [DOC-APP-COPILOT]. It can also draft a work order with the asset, urgency, recommended check, evidence IDs, and safety prerequisites, but it is only a draft and is never sent to a CMMS [DOC-APP-WORKORDER]. It answers other questions from retrieved documents and the selected asset’s evidence, and it gives no repair or disassembly procedures [DOC-APP-COPILOT].

faq.q: Is the hosted demo using live AI?
faq.text: No, the hosted demo does not use live AI; it uses pre-generated answers for common questions or document search instead. [DOC-APP-COPILOT] The copilot text also says the hosted demo has no live AI, while the backend-run version is where a live LLM writes answers. [DOC-APP-COPILOT]

faq.q: Can the app control plant equipment?
alts: does it write to the plant
faq.text: No, the app has no connection to plant controls and has no write path back into plant systems, so it cannot control equipment [DOC-APP-OVERVIEW][DOC-APP-INTEGRATION]. It is a browser pre-visit copilot for reading data, highlighting, planning, and drafting only, and any work-order content is just a draft for approval, not a control action [DOC-APP-OVERVIEW][DOC-APP-WORKORDER].

faq.q: What would a pilot measure?
faq.text: A pilot would measure object-identification precision and recall, the share of target assets found correctly, time to find equipment, time to prepare a maintenance visit, planning collisions or access problems caught before the visit, technician training performance, time to assemble a remote-support case, start-up time and frame rate, technician confidence and usability ratings, and agreement or false alarms versus technician outcomes. [DOC-APP-PILOT] It would also use replayed real data before any live connection. [DOC-APP-PILOT]

faq.q: How would it connect to real plant data?
faq.text:
It would connect through read-only adapters, not direct control links: OPC UA for current values and alarms, a historian read API for telemetry baselines, MQTT Sparkplug B subscriptions, a CMMS or EAM read API, and a document-management read API [DOC-APP-INTEGRATION]. 
Each adapter would map external identifiers to asset IDs through a reviewed mapping table and attach provenance such as source, observed time, received time, and live or replayed status [DOC-APP-INTEGRATION]. 
There is no write path back into plant systems, and the tool says there is no live plant data, no historian, and no CMMS connection in the current build [DOC-APP-INTEGRATION] [DOC-APP-DATA].

faq.q: What are the main limitations of the prototype?
faq.text:
The main limitations are that the prototype uses synthetic asset data, has no live plant data, historian, or CMMS connection, and the scan is never changed. [DOC-APP-DATA] [DOC-APP-COPILOT] 
Its layout, object labels, asset-to-object mapping, and plan simulation are approximate, and the Plan mode is only a maintenance-planning simulation, not an engineering clearance or installation check. [DOC-APP-DATA] [DOC-APP-PLAN] 
It also has no live multi-user session, no video, and no connection to plant controls, and the hosted demo may use pre-generated answers rather than live AI. [DOC-APP-SUPPORT] [DOC-APP-COPILOT]

faq.text: The Value page is an illustrative calculator with editable, clearly hypothetical inputs such as technicians, look-ups per week, weeks, and minutes before and after. faq.q: Can I create a work order?
faq.text: Yes — the copilot can draft a work order, but it is only a draft and needs planner approval; it is never sent to a CMMS and does no control action [DOC-APP-WORKORDER]. It can include the asset, inspection, urgency-based priority, recommended check, evidence IDs, and safety prerequisites such as work permit, isolation and lockout/tagout, OEM or site-approved procedure, and qualified personnel [DOC-APP-WORKORDER]. If you are using Support mode, the draft can be shared back in a support package for review, with no live session or plant control connection [DOC-APP-SUPPORT].

faq.q: What safety rules apply before working on equipment?
alts: is it safe to work on it
faq.text: Before working on equipment, use a work permit, isolation and lockout/tagout, an OEM or site-approved procedure, and qualified personnel under site procedures [DOC-APP-WORKORDER]. The assistant cannot judge something safe; that decision belongs to site procedures and qualified personnel [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY]. If you need to verify a specific asset, the context only contains general safety guardrails and synthetic asset/fleet data, not an OEM manual [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY][DOC-APP-DATA][DOC-APP-LIBRARY].

faq.q: What is fouling in a process pump?
faq.text:
In a process pump, fouling means internal deposits or build-up are narrowing the hydraulic path, so the pump moves less liquid and loses efficiency. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#casing] [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#impeller] 
The training notes link fouling to the casing or impeller, with signs like lower flow, lower pressure, or higher motor current for the same duty. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#casing] [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#impeller] 
In the fleet table, P-005 is marked as a process pump with issue fouling and an efficiency-loss summary, which matches that general meaning. [ASSET-017]

faq.q: What is cavitation risk?
faq.text: Cavitation risk is a hydraulic instability that can make a process pump behave like it is starving or flashing, and the evidence marks it as high severity or medium severity depending on the case [CASE-049] [CASE-026] [CASE-022]. The related pump note says cavitation can cause erosion at the impeller vane inlets and pitting in the volute casing, with symptoms tied to flow, pressure, motor current, and vibration signals [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#impeller] [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#casing]. For the selected fleet, P-002 has a cavitation risk issue and attention required status, with high urgency and 14 open alarms/events [ASSET-014]. The tool cannot judge whether the asset is safe; that decision belongs to site procedures and qualified personnel, with verification and escalation under lockout/tagout [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY].

faq.q: What does misalignment look like in the data?
faq.text:
Misalignment looks like a rotating-equipment alignment signature with vibration, often axial or at 2×, and it may also show element wear or higher motor current. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#coupling] 
For pumps and motors, the data pattern is usually vibration_mm_s, sometimes with motor_current_a, and the cases describe it as a coupling or alignment-related vibration pattern. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#coupling][CASE-041][CASE-046] 
Soft foot or loose anchoring can point toward misalignment and vibration as well. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#baseplate]

faq.q: What is current imbalance in a motor?
faq.text: Current imbalance in a motor means the motor current is uneven across phases, often called phase-to-phase imbalance or current/load imbalance [KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#stator_windings][KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#terminal_box][KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#motor]. It can point to issues such as stator winding insulation ageing, loose or corroded terminals, broken rotor bars, or load-related imbalance [KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#stator_windings][KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#terminal_box][KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#rotor][KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#motor]. The context includes synthetic asset examples where M-004 and M-005 are marked with current imbalance, but no live plant data or a specific selected asset is provided [ASSET-022][ASSET-023][DOC-APP-DATA].

faq.q: What causes a control valve position deviation?
faq.text:
Common causes in the context are friction or stiction, calibration drift, feedback linkage wear, air relay faults, loose mounting, actuator spring fatigue, abnormal load, supply pressure issues, and device alerts; these are investigation signals, not proof by themselves. [DOC-CONTROL_VALVE-CORE] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#positioner] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#spring] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#yoke] 
For control valves, the positioner, actuator spring, and yoke are named as likely contributors to position deviation. [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#positioner] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#spring] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#yoke] 
The fleet table also shows control valves with position deviation or calibration drift, including CV-003, CV-009, and CV-007. [ASSET-003] [ASSET-009] [ASSET-007]

faq.q: What is calibration drift?
faq.text:
Calibration drift means the asset’s measured position slowly stops matching the true or expected position over time, so the reading no longer lines up with the baseline or reference. [CASE-033] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#positioner] 
For CV-007, the evidence says “position calibration drift” with the next check to verify calibration, and its condition is watch with health 71. [DOC-ASSET-007] [ASSET-007] 
The context also says to review trend and events, compare to baseline, and follow approved safety and maintenance procedures. [CASE-033]

faq.q: What is a vibration sensor mounting issue?
faq.text: A vibration sensor mounting issue is a problem with how the sensor is attached to the machine, so the mounting is not giving a stable, rigid connection and the reading quality can drop [KB-XRAY-VIBRATION_SENSOR#mounting_stud, DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE]. Typical signs are loose mounting, wrong torque, signal drift, missing data, or poor signal quality, and it can reduce confidence in the vibration data [KB-XRAY-VIBRATION_SENSOR#mounting_stud, DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE]. The context also shows this as a mounting-quality signature with the next check being to inspect sensor mounting, while following approved safety and maintenance procedures [CASE-015]. For the fleet, VS-002 is listed with issue mounting issue and VS-003 is listed as normal [ASSET-029, ASSET-030].

faq.q: Why do data-quality issues lower confidence?
faq.text: Data-quality issues lower confidence because the confidence formula explicitly multiplies by one minus a data-quality penalty, so worse data reduces the final score [DOC-APP-DIAGNOSIS]. Poor signal quality, drift, missing data, or bad mounting also mean the sensor evidence is less reliable, so downstream confidence should drop [DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE]. The context also says stale or poor-quality data lowers confidence [DOC-APP-INTEGRATION].

faq.q: Which assets have high vibration?
faq.text: The assets with the clearest high vibration-related evidence are P-005 and M-001 [ASSET-017, ASSET-019]. P-005 is a process pump with a severity high bearing wear case and a summary of efficiency loss / fouling-like signature [CASE-050, ASSET-017]. M-001 is an electric motor with a misalignment issue and a coupling/alignment-related vibration pattern [ASSET-019]. The context also lists VS-002 as a degraded vibration sensor with a mounting issue, but not as high vibration itself [ASSET-029].

faq.q: How was the 3D scan processed?
faq.text: The 3D scan was processed as a Gaussian-splat model of the equipment room, with the floor leveled by a RANSAC floor plane and the walls axis-aligned [DOC-APP-SCAN]. It is treated as approximately metric, but the scale was not surveyed [DOC-APP-SCAN]. The browser renders 1,669,970 splats with view-dependent colour as compressed chunks, while phones load the most important 730 thousand splats [DOC-APP-SCAN]. A 2D floor plan replaces the 3D view when WebGL 2 is missing, and an earlier corrupt file is not used [DOC-APP-SCAN].

faq.q: Does it work without a GPU or on a phone?
faq.text: Yes, it works without a GPU in the browser, because the 3D view falls back to a 2D floor plan when WebGL 2 is missing. On phones, it loads the most important 730 thousand splats, so it is supported there too [DOC-APP-SCAN]. The same planner runs in the browser as a JavaScript port, and the scan integrity notes say the environment is a Gaussian-splat scan with valid records [DOC-APP-NAV, DOC-APP-SCAN].

faq.q: What should a technician do on arrival at P-005?
alts: what to do when I get there
faq.text: On arrival at P-005, the technician should confirm the asset identity on site using the tag, QR, or NFC before acting, then review the trend and events and compare against baseline under approved safety procedures [DOC-ASSET-017][CASE-025][DOC-FIELD-SAFETY]. The next check is to inspect the hydraulic path, because P-005 is an attention required process pump with a fouling-like signature and high urgency [DOC-ASSET-017][ASSET-017]. Do not open or adjust the equipment without permit, isolation, and lockout/tagout; that decision belongs to site procedures and qualified personnel [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY].

faq.q: Which alarms are open?
faq.text: The context does not list the specific open alarm names or tags, only counts of open alarms and high-severity alarms by asset [ASSET-017] [ASSET-003] [ASSET-016] [ASSET-024]. It does show that P-005 has 6 open alarms and 3 high-severity open alarms, CV-003 has 7 and 1, P-004 has 8 and 2, and M-006 has 5 and 1 [ASSET-017] [ASSET-003] [ASSET-016] [ASSET-024]. If you need the alarm names, the context does not contain them [ASSET-017] [ASSET-003] [ASSET-016] [ASSET-024].

faq.q: Who should I escalate to?
faq.text: Escalate through site procedures to qualified personnel responsible for the affected asset, and use lockout/tagout and permits as required; the tool cannot judge safety or replace that decision [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY]. For P-005, the evidence shows attention required, high urgency, fouling-like signature, six open alarms, and three high-severity events, so verification and escalation are warranted [ASSET-017]. If you need a remote hand-off, Support mode is the documented expert escalation path, but it is not a live plant-control channel [DOC-APP-SUPPORT].

faq.q: How are similar historical cases used?
faq.text: Similar historical cases are used as one of the evidence inputs when the engine builds a diagnosis for an asset, along with state, telemetry, alarms, work orders, data quality, and documents. [DOC-APP-DIAGNOSIS] They are specifically historical service cases of the same class and issue, so they support the hypotheses and confidence shown in the result. [DOC-APP-DIAGNOSIS] The context does not include the individual case details, only that 50 historical service cases are in the library. [DOC-APP-LIBRARY]

faq.text: The library contains the builder pack’s knowledge documents, 30 asset cards, 50 historical service cases, 49 component training notes for the illustrative X-Ray models, and the product documentation of this prototype [DOC-APP-LIBRARY]. It includes the field-safety guardrail, the evidence-grounded response contract, and the 3D mapping contract, plus the core diagnostic context per equipment type [DOC-APP-LIBRARY].
